correctness.rationale: The matching model and induced-count normalization are fully defined. Conditioning on a fixed isolated chord gives two independent uniform submatchings, so connected induced motifs cannot cross the split; count endpoint pairs to derive the exact finite sum. Vandermonde gives termwise strict negativity. Adjacent chords dominate the fixed-r asymptotic and an explicit ratio bound controls the nonadjacent remainder. The extracted executable checker passed 684 exact assertions through all 10,395 six-chord matchings; these finite checks are corroborative, not an infinite proof.

The historical simple-chord/crossing generating polynomial yields a covariance for adjacent chords only, not nonadjacent isolated chord events or arbitrary connected induced motifs.

value.rationale: The theorem determines the exact finite-size normalized dependence, shared by every connected realizable induced circle-graph motif of the same size, with a universal strict negative sign and leading rate. A disconnected-motif counterexample proves connectivity is not a cosmetic condition; this is a general local-global dependence law rather than a single routine case.
